chunks: From him, from al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the minimum amount in which the thief's hand is cut off. He said: 'In the egg of iron.' I said: 'And what is its price?' He said: 'One-quarter of a dinar.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The thief is not cut off until his theft reaches one-quarter of a dinar.' And indeed, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) cut off [the hand] for the egg of iron.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.بَيضَةِ حَدِيدٍ: Egg of iron (a specific weight/value measure)
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: Is cut off (referring to the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen goods required for cutting the thief's hand in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar defines the nisab for hadd al-sariqa as one-quarter of a dinar, equated to the value of an 'egg of iron' (baydat hadid), a standard measure in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the jurisprudential distinction between the absolute minimum threshold for punishment and the practical application by Imam Ali (AS), who may have applied cutting for lesser values based on judicial discretion (ra'y) or specific contexts, illustrating the flexibility of the Imam's authority in implementing divine law.
